name: Hip Adduction
definition: A strict unilateral open-chain hip isolation performed standing with both hands on stable external support and an elastic band cuffed at the working ankle. The straight working leg begins in maximal comfortable abduction and moves medially while a slight posterior hip posture is held, finishing one foot-width lateral to the stance foot. The sources report an approximately half-foot-length posterior endpoint but do not quantify the three-dimensional start path; the active record therefore standardizes that posterior posture throughout as a disclosed mechanics-derived adaptation so hip extension does not become an undeclared prime action. The visible adductor-longus/brevis region is primary because the exercise study measured adductor longus; the combined body-model region cannot display the two muscles separately. Gracilis is a mechanics-derived secondary because it produces hip adduction while also controlling the straight loaded knee. Gluteus medius is a directly measured hip-and-pelvis stabilizer. Rectus abdominis and the combined obliques region stabilize the trunk; only external oblique was measured, so internal-oblique credit is an explicit taxonomy aggregation rather than direct evidence. Adductor magnus, pectineus, and other capable regions remain unassigned rather than receiving volume from anatomy capability alone. Side-lying, Copenhagen, ball-squeeze, cable, machine, bodyweight, internally or externally rotated, closed-chain, and multi-joint variants remain outside this contract.

exercises.name: Supported Standing Band Hip Adduction
exercises.movementDefinition: Stand upright on the support leg while holding a stable external support with both hands and secure an elastic band around the working ankle from the side. Place the straight working leg in maximal comfortable abduction with tension already in the band and hold it at the same slight posterior hip posture used at the endpoint. Keep the pelvis still, the working knee straight, and both sets of toes pointing forward as you draw the working thigh medially without swinging it farther backward, finishing one foot-width lateral to and about half a foot-length behind the stance foot. Return under control along the same strictly frontal path, then repeat before changing sides.
